text:
Aaron: Great runtime segment today — a couple quick clarifying Qs for folks working on the roadmap: 

1) Microbatching targets: what's the recommended max batch for latency-sensitive chat routes vs high-throughput embedding routes?
2) KV cache semantics: are we doing strict per-session isolation or best-effort shared prefix caching for cost savings? Any consistency caveats?
3) Kernel canary ownership: who is the primary for initiating canaries, and who has the authority to force an immediate revert?
4) Telemetry: product needs a concise set of signals to show to PMs (one graph for latency and one for cost). What do you recommend?

Leila: Short answers from runtime lead: 
- Microbatching: default max for chat routes = 8 (aim p95 < 80ms). For high-throughput text/embeddings we use 64+ (throughput optimized). We also support multi-tier per-route override.
- KV cache: per-session pinning for the first 2-5 minutes, then best-effort shared prefix cache. We avoid strong consistency guarantees — treat cache as performance hint, not source-of-truth. Eviction is size-based LRU with TTL.
- Canary ownership: runtime eng (me + oncall lead) kicks canaries; SRE/infra can forcibly rollback. Anyone can request rollback but SRE makes the call when thresholds hit.
- Telemetry: keep it to three curves: p50/p95 token-latency, request success rate, and cost per 1k tokens (or per-request cost). Add traffic fraction by model-variant as a fourth if helpful.

Chen: Adding quick numbers from last week's staging run (gpu-pool-beta, single-token continuations):
- chat batch=8 -> p50 10ms, p95 42ms, p99 140ms
- chat batch=16 -> p50 14ms, p95 70ms, p99 260ms
- embeddings batch=128 -> p50 210ms, p95 700ms (larger I/O pattern)
Note: we saw a memory spike in batch=64 chat runs on V100 nodes; mitigated by kernel memory watermarks.

Marco: For product: helpful. Can we standardize the telemetry dashboard name so PMs don't hunt? Also, when you say "per-route override" — can product toggle that, or is it infra-only?

Leila: We'll publish a canonical dashboard: "Runtime / Route SLOs (Latency | Cost)". Per-route overrides require infra access today — we can add a lighter toggle in Console for product later (feature request tracked).

OpsBot: Canary scheduled: canary/2213456789 at 2026-04-05T18:30:00Z. Alerts: runtime-canary-latency, runtime-canary-memory, runtime-canary-errors.

Aaron: Leila, can you paste the minimal canary config we should put into the roadmap doc? Chen, can you link the staging run dashboard?

Leila: Minimal canary snippet: 
```
canary:
  traffic_fraction: 0.05
  duration_minutes: 30
  sample_rate_traces: 1.0
  fallback_policy:
    latency_threshold_ms: 500
    consecutive_window_seconds: 30
    fallback_variant: quantized-v1
```

Chen: Staging run dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/gpu-beta/runtime-batch-staging (contains histograms, memory traces).

Marco: I'll add the dashboard link and Leila's snippet to the roadmap doc and tag runtime leads. Also adding a product ask: surface per-route batch size in Console.

Leila: Thanks — if folks have representative prompts for prewarm/canary tests, paste them here. We prefer 1 short convo, 1 long context (~1500 tokens), and one high-throughput embedding batch.

Aaron: Dropping quick prompts: "Summarize the conversation in 1 sentence." + a lorem ipsum 1500-token repeat + 128 JSON blobs for embeddings.

Leila: Perfect. I'll coordinate with SRE to run the canary and post results in this thread. Closing for initial follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
